title: fix(core): narrow validateSchema's published parameter to unknown
body:
Fixes #8416

`validateSchema` in `@object-ui/core` took `schema: any` — a bare `any` on a published
parameter. This narrows it to `unknown` and makes the implementation narrow the value
before it reads a key off it.

## The card's premise, measured before relying on it

The card graded this cheap on one argument: for a **parameter**, `any` to `unknown` is
caller-compatible, so the cost lands inside the implementation. It supplied its own
falsifier — *if the return type or generics thread the parameter's `any` outward, it stops
being caller-compatible*. Measured, not inherited:

| reading | result |
|---|---|
| generics on `validateSchema` | none — the function is not generic |
| return type | the concrete `SchemaNodeValidationResult`, which names no parameter type |
| published declaration delta | one token: `validateSchema(schema: any, path?: string)` becomes `validateSchema(schema: unknown, path?: string)` |
| new exported symbols | none — `SchemaNodeUnderValidation` and `isSchemaNodeShape` are module-private and appear in no published `.d.ts` (grepped across every `packages/*/dist`) |
| call sites outside `packages/core` | one: `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx:84`, which passes a value already typed `any`. It needed no change — `@object-ui/react` `type-check` and its two `SchemaRenderer` suites (49 tests) pass untouched |

**The falsifier does not fire, and the re-grade trigger was not hit.** No call site outside
this package moved.

## The half that is not a type annotation

`validateSchema` calls four rules unconditionally and only **one** of them ever checked it
had an object. `validateBaseSchema` refused a non-object and returned; `validateRetiredNodeType`
used optional chaining; but `validateFormSchema` read `schema.type` and `validateChildren`
read `schema.children` straight through. So, measured on `256c709e2` before the change:

```
validateSchema(null)       ->  TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'type')
validateSchema(undefined)  ->  TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'type')
isValidSchema(null)        ->  the same TypeError, from a function documented "@returns True if the value is a valid schema"
assertValidSchema(null)    ->  the same TypeError, in place of its own `Schema validation failed:` refusal
```

`SchemaRenderer` wraps its call in a `try`/`catch` commented *"Validator itself failed —
surface but don't crash render"*. That catch is where the crash was landing in the one
shipped consumer.

The guard now runs **once**, in `validateSchema`, before any rule reads a key; the four
rules take a narrowed node type whose keys are all `unknown`. The same defect one level
down goes with it: a `null` entry inside a form's `fields` array threw the same way.

## Accept-set delta — 29 cases, diffed before and after

Both matrices were produced from a real build: the pre-change one by restoring the base
file, rebuilding `@object-ui/core`, confirming the mutation reached `dist/` (`dist` declared
`validateSchema(schema: any`), then probing.

**25 of 29 identical.** The four that moved:

| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `null` | THREW `TypeError` | `INVALID_SCHEMA` at `schema` |
| `undefined` | THREW `TypeError` | `INVALID_SCHEMA` at `schema` |
| `{ type: 'form', fields: [null] }` | THREW `TypeError` | `MISSING_FIELD_NAME` at `schema.fields[0]` |
| `{ type: 'form', fields: [namedFunction] }` | `valid: true` | `MISSING_FIELD_NAME` at `schema.fields[0]` |

The first three are a crash becoming the documented refusal. **The fourth is a genuine
refusal-set widening** and it is why this is declared `Clause-②: yes` below: a named
function satisfied `field.name` through `Function.prototype.name`. It is a corner JSON
cannot express, and function values on this family's mirrors are already refused
(objectui#6124) — but that changeset names `@object-ui/types`' zod `validateSchema`, not
this structural one, so there is no published contract text that already covers it.

Everything else holds: an array node keeps `MISSING_REQUIRED` (`typeof []` is `'object'`,
and the replaced guard let it through too), primitives keep their single `INVALID_SCHEMA`,
`null` holes inside `children` are still skipped, the `body` dialect still resolves, nested
retired types are still refused by path, and no new error `code` is emitted.

## Verification

Every command was run from the repo root. Readings are quoted from each tool's own verdict
line, and the union below was run at `f5cb148f5`, the final commit.

**Ablation — from the committed tree, mutation proved on disk first.** The mutation is
`git checkout 256c709e2 -- packages/core/src/validation/schema-validator.ts`, i.e. reverting
the narrowing wholesale.

- on-disk proof: marker `isSchemaNodeShape` 7 to 0, `schema: unknown` 1 to 0; blob hash
  `3802177` to `e27f547`, equal to the base blob and different from the head blob.
- the vitest leg resolves `../schema-validator.js` to package **source**, not `dist` — no
  build sits between the mutation and the run.
- **6 tests go red, by name:**
  - `takes every value UNCAST, which is what makes the narrowing caller-compatible`
  - `` `validateSchema(null)` returns INVALID_SCHEMA instead of throwing a raw TypeError ``
  - `` `validateSchema(undefined)` returns INVALID_SCHEMA instead of throwing a raw TypeError ``
  - `` `isValidSchema(null)` answers `false`, which is the boolean its docblock promises ``
  - `` `assertValidSchema(null)` throws the validator's OWN refusal, not a TypeError ``
  - ``a `null` entry inside `fields` is REPORTED, not thrown on``
- **control: 138 tests stay green**, including all 64 pre-existing tests in
  `schema-validator.test.ts`, `predicate-valued-gate-rules.test.ts` and
  `form-field-widget-namespace.test.ts`, plus this file's own five behaviour-preservation
  cases. The mutation is surgical; the harness is live.
- restored **by state**: `git diff HEAD` empty and the blob back at `3802177`.

**The type-level half fires under `tsc`, not vitest, and is shown doing it.** The pin is a
compile-time refusal (the mechanism objectui#3181 established for this package), and
`tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` confirms the file is in that program (1 hit of 234).
Under the same mutation:

```
src/validation/__tests__/unknown-schema-param-8416.test.ts(74,11): error TS2322: Type 'true' is not assignable to type 'never'.
```

**Gate enumeration, on both axes.** Asked *which tests read this file or path*, and
separately *what lines did my change move*.

- *Content axis.* `scripts/__tests__/body-dialect-census.test.ts:198` asserts this file still
  contains the literal `schema.children || schema.body`. It does — the narrowing kept that
  expression byte-identical. Green.
- *Position axis.* `scripts/check-doc-example-types.mjs` keys its ledger by `path:line symbol`,
  and two rows point into this file. My diff moved both JSDoc blocks down, so the rows were
  re-derived from the file: `490` to `550` (`assertValidSchema`) and `515` to `575`
  (`isValidSchema`). Verdicts and codes unchanged. Same precedent as the objectui#8738 row
  already in that file.
  **Control that moves when the change is wrong:** reverting just the `550` row back to `490`
  makes `check:doc-examples` exit 1 with `STALE LEDGER ROW ...:490 assertValidSchema` and
  `UNDECLARED FAILURE ...:550 assertValidSchema`. The row edit is load-bearing, not cosmetic.

**Runs.**

| command | verdict |
|---|---|
| `turbo run build $(node scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs --build-filter) --concurrency=2` | `35 successful, 35 total` |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core run type-check` | exit 0 (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/react run type-check` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/src/validation/` | `Test Files 8 passed · Tests 144 passed` |
| `pnpm exec vitest run` on the two `SchemaRenderer` gate-diagnostic suites | `Tests 49 passed` |
| `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/body-dialect-census.test.ts scripts/__tests__/check-doc-example-types.test.ts scripts/__tests__/check-doc-example-shared-reader.test.ts` | `Test Files 3 passed · Tests 87 passed` |
| `node scripts/check-doc-example-types.mjs` | exit 0 — *"Every covered `@example` compiles, or fails exactly as its ledger row declares."* |
| `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | exit 0 — `scanned 7072 tracked text file(s)` |

**Lint — the complete units, not a narrowing.** CI's lint job runs `pnpm lint` (turbo, per
package) plus `lint:root`. My diff lives in exactly two of those units and both were run
whole: `@object-ui/core` (**234 files**, 0 errors) and the root scope (**305 files**, 0
errors, and `scripts/check-doc-example-types.mjs` confirmed present in the population).
File counts are read from eslint's own `--format json` output. Type-aware linting is not
enabled anywhere in `eslint.config.js` (zero occurrences of `project`), so this diff cannot
move the verdict of any file it does not itself contain — the other package units are
provably unaffected rather than merely unrun. The five surviving
`@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` warnings in this file are all pre-existing and on lines
this diff does not touch; the file's bare `: any` count drops 13 to 5.

**Ratchets: none moved, measured.** `KNOWN_BARE_ANY_EXAMPLES` in
`scripts/check-skill-examples.mjs` is an empty set whose `SCAN_ROOTS` are `skills` and
`.claude/skills` — it cannot see `packages/**`. A repo-wide grep for `BARE_ANY` / `bare-any`
finds that script and its own test and nothing else, so there is no other bare-`any` ratchet
to move. No baseline was edited.

**Governed surface: none touched.** `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on
all four changed paths answers `NOT GOVERNED — 4 path(s) checked against 5 governed
surface(s); none matched.`

## Clause-②: yes

Judged here, not inherited. The mechanical floor is clear: **no** new exported symbol and
**no** new key on a published payload (both grepped, above). What tips it is the fourth row
of the accept-set matrix — one input that validated before and is refused now. A `no` would
have to cite published contract text that already declares that refusal; objectui#6124 is
the closest and it names a different symbol in a different package. Genuinely unsure, so:
`yes`. The `needs:contract-review` label is on this PR and on the card.

⚠️ The `Clause-②:` line could not be added to the claim comment — the dispatching seat has
no comment-edit tool (objectstack#17213) — so this section and the report are where the
declaration lives. A second claim comment was deliberately **not** posted.

⚠️ `node scripts/pm/check-widening-tells.mjs` was **not** used as evidence. Its bare CLI has
no repo flag and always judges as objectstack (objectstack#17217), and using the exported
judge with `repo` set correctly does not rescue it here: the control fires as expected
(`packages/types/src/zod/form.zod.ts` is covered as objectui, not covered as objectstack),
and under that same correct repo **none** of this diff's four files is covered by any
surface row. The tool has nothing to say about these paths in either direction.

## 验收备注

Observations found while reading the file. None is filed, and none is in this PR.

- `assertValidSchema(schema: any)` and `isValidSchema(value: any)` sit directly below
  `validateSchema` in the same file and are the same class — published parameters typed
  bare `any`. They were left alone deliberately: the card scopes to `validateSchema`, and
  narrowing two more published parameters is a second published-surface change on a card
  graded p3. `assertValidSchema`'s ledger row already declares TS18046 (`is of type
  'unknown'`), so touching it would also move a declared diagnostic. **Successor: #7493**,
  the parent bare-`any` census. *noted, not filed.*
- The three `BASE_SCHEMA_RULES` validators still read `validate: (value: any)`, while
  `predicateGateRule` next to them already reads `(value: unknown)`. They consume
  `schema[key]`, which this change made `unknown`, and each narrows with `typeof` on its
  first line, so nothing is unsound — it is an inconsistency the file's own
  `AuthoredFormField` docblock already notes ("The rest of this file predates that
  discipline"). **Successor: #7493.** *noted, not filed.*
- `validateSchema([])` reports `MISSING_REQUIRED` rather than "schema must be an object",
  because `typeof []` is `'object'`. Preserved exactly, and pinned by a test in this PR so
  it cannot drift silently. Whether an array node deserves its own refusal is a product
  question, not a defect. *noted, not filed.*
- The two ledger rows this PR re-derived are keyed by line number and share no vocabulary
  with their subject — the class objectui#8875 was filed for this shift. No cross-file
  `path:line` address was written into any comment added here; the ledger comment names the
  moves in the file that owns them. *noted, not filed.*
